text: Sleep diary, as promised. I'm 34, and for the last fortnight I've been getting to sleep around 1 a.m. and waking at 5:30, so roughly four and a half hours, though last Tuesday it might have been five, no wait, closer to four. I do not nap in the day and I have stopped coffee after noon. No sleeping tablets, nothing prescribed. My flatmate Sigrid says I talk in my sleep, which I can't confirm either way. Mood is flat but not low, and I haven't had any thoughts of self-harm. Weekends are better, about seven hours, I think.

task: Check the arithmetic and tell me whether rounding the dose to a measurable volume would be sensible.
text: Check my arithmetic on this practice problem for my pharmacology module (it's from the course workbook, not a real patient). A syrup is labelled 125 mg per 5 ml. The textbook says to give 15 mg per kg per day, divided into three doses, for a child weighing 18 kg. So the daily total is 270 mg, each dose is 90 mg, and 90 mg is 3.6 ml. I got 3.6 ml but then second-guessed myself because one of the old exam papers had 4 ml. I also assumed we shouldn't round to the nearest 0.5 ml. Is that assumption sensible, or should I round to something a syringe can actually measure?

task: Turn this into a short summary for the trip coordinator: the permission, the medical points and who to call in an emergency. Her age isn't needed.
text:
Dear Mr Whitlock,

Thank you for the trip letter. Imogen is 11, so she's in the Year 6 residential group, and I'm giving permission for the full three nights, not just two. She has a nut allergy (EpiPen in her bag) and gets travel-sick on coaches, so please seat Imogen near the front. Her dad, Callum, works away on weeks when I'm on shift at the hospital, so for emergencies please try me first, then Callum. Is the final payment 85 or 95? Your letter says both on different pages.

Kind regards,
Clémence
